analysis:
Examined the three StandaloneServer.swift head units and the two LaunchAgent.swift units (the first is metadata only). The changed StandaloneServer.swift lines are 1538-1541, 1546-1550 and 1557-1564. In ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad, a one-time reclaim now runs before LRU eviction when busy engines retain reclaimable memory. The new releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad calls GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then MLX.Memory.clearCache(), gated by nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed. The callers run under the isLoadingAny serialization. I found no new authorization, attestation or encryption path. The change only affects memory accounting and availability (T-029 and TB-007 resource handling). The loop remains bounded: poolDropped is set once, and eviction or a capacityUnavailable throw follows.

LaunchAgent.swift adds three env keys to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys: idleCacheSweep, segmentRetention and segmentHostZeros. These are rollback knobs for the idle-gated cache sweep and for retained, host-zeroed paged KV segments. Passing them into the launchd provider job is operator-controlled, local, and consistent with the existing keys. The names are non-secret.

Open question for integration, outside the supplied evidence: retaining free KV segments across requests (GlobalKVCacheBudget and EngineV2Factory, not supplied) touches T-028, residual KV data in GPU memory. The documentation says the segments are host-zeroed and that the host-zero toggle is the rollback, but I could not verify that zeroing occurs before a segment is reused by another tenant. The disabling env var is not an attestation-covered input, which is the same trust level as the other passthrough keys under TB-003. A reviewer of those unsupplied files should confirm that segment reuse zeroes the data and that retained segments never reach the SSD cache path or the T-041 surfaces. There is no concrete regression in the supplied diff.
